transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Yeah… I guess I’m here because I just haven’t been feeling right for a long time. Most days I wake up and it’s like there’s already this gray weight sitting on me before I even get out of bed. I go to work, I’m out there with the crew doing landscaping, trying to keep moving, and I’m around my kids too, but even then it’s like I can’t really shake it.

It’s not just a bad mood that passes. It’s more like this low, hollow feeling, like I’m there physically but I’m just going through the motions. I keep trying to push through because that’s what I’ve always done, but lately it feels heavy enough that I figured I probably needed to talk to somebody.
How long have you been feeling this way?

It’s been… a little over three years now. About three years and three months, if I’m really thinking about it.

I can kind of trace it back to when the groundskeeping contract changed our schedule. The longer days just took over everything, and after that it felt like I never really got back to myself. At first I thought I was just worn out and needed to get used to it, but then months kept passing, and then years, and it was still there. So yeah… around three years and some change.
Do you find yourself enjoying activities that you used to like before you started feeling this way?

I’m not really sure how to answer that cleanly. I mean… I know there are things I used to do, or things that were supposed to feel good, but I don’t know if I’ve sat down and measured it that way, you know?

Some days I’ll still do the same stuff because it’s part of life, or because other people are doing it, but whether I’m enjoying it the way I used to… I don’t know. It’s kind of hard for me to separate “not enjoying it” from just being tired or distracted or whatever else is going on in my head. I guess I’d have to think more about what I used to like before all this and compare it, because right now it all sort of blends together.
Do you feel like you've lost interest in things you used to enjoy?

I’m honestly not sure. I know that sounds like I’m dodging the question, but I don’t mean to be. It’s just hard for me to tell what counts as “lost interest” versus me just not having the energy or not being able to get my head into things the way I used to.

Like, there are things I still do because they’re there, because it’s routine, or because people expect me to show up for them. But if you asked me whether I’m sitting there thinking, “Yeah, I really enjoy this,” I don’t know. I don’t check in with myself that way much. Most of the time I’m just trying to get through the day and do what I’m supposed to do.

So… maybe? But I can’t say it clearly. It’s more like everything feels kind of muted, and I’m not sure if that means I lost interest or if I’m just worn down.
Can you think of anything recently that you've done and actually felt pleasure or enjoyment from?

I’m trying to think of something, and nothing really jumps out at me. Not in a clear way, anyway.

Like, I do things during the week, I go through the motions, and sometimes something is… fine, I guess. But if you mean actual pleasure, like I felt lighter or glad I was doing it, I’m not sure I can point to anything recent and say, “Yes, that was it.” I don’t really keep track of it, and when I look back, the days kind of run together.

There might be small moments where I’m not feeling as weighed down, but I don’t know if that counts as enjoyment. It’s more like, “Okay, this isn’t terrible,” not really something I’d call pleasure. So… I don’t know. I can’t think of anything specific right now.
Have you ever thought about ending your life?

I… I don’t know how to answer that exactly. I mean, that’s a heavy question, and I’m not trying to be difficult. I just don’t know if what’s gone through my head is the same as what you mean by “thought about ending my life.”

Sometimes when I’m really worn down, I’ll have thoughts like I don’t want to keep doing everything, or I wish I could just not have to deal with anything for a while. But I don’t know if that’s the same thing as actually thinking about ending my life. I don’t really have a clean answer where I can say yes or no and feel like I’m being accurate.

It’s more like… I get overwhelmed, and my mind goes to dark places, but I’m not sure how to describe it without making it sound more definite than it is. I guess I’d need you to explain what you mean a little more, because I don’t want to say the wrong thing.
Have you ever had thoughts of actually taking your own life, not just wishing you didn't have to deal with things?

I’m… I’m not sure. I know you’re trying to separate it out, and I get why, but even with you saying it that way, I still have a hard time knowing how to answer without making it sound like something very specific.

I’ve had dark thoughts, yeah, and I’ve had moments where things feel so heavy that my mind goes somewhere ugly. But when you say “actually taking my own life,” like forming that thought in a clear way, I don’t know. I can’t honestly sit here and say, “Yes, I’ve had that exact thought,” because I don’t know that I have in a way I could point to. But I also don’t want to say “no” too quickly, because then it feels like I’m brushing off how bad it can get in my head sometimes.

It’s more like… I’ll get to a place where I just want everything to stop, or I don’t want to be in my own life for a while, if that makes sense. But whether that crosses into actually thinking, “I’m going to take my own life,” I don’t know. I don’t have a clear memory of planning it out or deciding something like that. It’s vague and scary and kind of hard to talk about.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight over the past three years?

I don’t think so… not a significant amount, at least not that I’ve noticed.

My weight goes up and down a little, I guess, like depending on how much I’m working or what I’m eating, but I haven’t had one of those situations where my clothes are suddenly hanging off me or people are commenting on it. I also don’t weigh myself very consistently, so I can’t give you an exact number over three years.

So, I’d say no major weight loss that I’m aware of.
Have you been having any problems with your sleep?

I’m not really sure how to answer that cleanly. I mean, I sleep, but I don’t know if I’d call it “problems” exactly without knowing what you mean.

Some nights are worse than others, and I don’t always feel like my sleep is doing what it’s supposed to do, if that makes sense. But I haven’t really kept track of it or anything. I’m not the kind of person who writes down when I go to bed or how many times I wake up, so I’d be guessing a little.

I guess I’d say… maybe, but I’m not sure how much of it counts as a sleep problem versus just regular life stuff or being tired from work. What kind of sleep problems are you asking about?
Do you often feel tired or lacking in energy?

Yeah… yes. That’s probably one of the bigger things, honestly.

It’s not just “I’m tired after work,” because I know landscaping is physical and I’m not twenty-five anymore. I expect to be worn out at the end of the day. But this is more like… by midmorning, sometimes, my body already feels like I’ve put in a full day. Like I’ll be loading tools or getting equipment together, and it feels heavier than it should, or I’m looking at the job plan and even that feels like it takes more out of me than it ought to.

And even on a Sunday, if I sleep in or try to catch up, I don’t really bounce back. I’ll still kind of drag through basic stuff—making dinner, putting things away, just getting myself moving. It’s like there’s not much in the tank to start with, and then the day barely has to begin before I’m already running low.
Do you feel more energized at any point in the day, or is the tiredness consistent from morning to night?

It’s pretty much most of the day, honestly. I don’t really have a part of the day where I’d say, “Oh, now I feel good, now I’ve got my energy back.”

Maybe right when I first get up I can tell myself, okay, let’s get moving, maybe today won’t be so bad. But it doesn’t last. By midmorning, a lot of days, my body feels like I’ve already put in a full day, even if I’m just loading tools or getting things organized. And it’s not only the physical stuff either—checking the job plan, figuring out what needs to happen first, even that can feel like it takes more effort than it should.

Then by the time I get home, I’m just dragging. And the frustrating part is, even if it’s Sunday and I sleep in, or I don’t have the usual workday, I still don’t really feel recharged. I can still drag through simple things like making dinner or picking up around the house. So yeah, I’d say it’s fairly consistent. It might get worse as the day goes on, but I don’t really get that clear “energized” part of the day.
Do you often feel guilty or worthless about things you've done or haven't done?

I don’t know… that’s a harder one to answer.

I mean, I can think of things I wish I’d handled better, sure. I think everybody can. I’ll look back on a conversation or something I didn’t get done and kind of chew on it more than I probably need to. But “worthless” feels like a big word, and I’m not sure I’d say it exactly like that.

Guilty… maybe sometimes, but I don’t know if it’s often in the way you mean. It’s more like I get frustrated with myself, like I should be doing better or keeping up better, and then I go around in circles about it. But I’m not sure if that counts as guilt or just being hard on myself.

So I guess I’d say I’m not really sure. I wouldn’t want to say yes too strongly and make it sound like something it isn’t, but I also wouldn’t say I never feel that way.
Do you have trouble concentrating or focusing on things?

I’m not really sure how to answer that one clearly.

I mean, I have days where I’ll be looking at something and realize I’m not really taking it in, but I don’t know if that’s concentration exactly or just… I don’t know, being worn down or distracted. Like if I’m reading through something or trying to figure out the order of what needs doing, sometimes I have to go back over it, but I don’t know that I’d say I have a major problem focusing.

At work, I usually still get through what I need to get through. I might be slower about it, or I’ll kind of stand there for a second trying to get myself organized, but I haven’t really thought of it as “I can’t concentrate.” It’s more like everything takes a little more pushing than it should.

So… maybe some trouble, but I’m not sure. It’s not something I’ve paid as much attention to as the tiredness.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite over the past three years?

I’m not really sure, honestly. I haven’t noticed a big, clear change where I could say, “Yeah, my appetite is definitely different now.”

Some days I don’t feel that interested in food, but I don’t know if that’s appetite changing or just me not wanting to deal with making something. Other days I eat normally enough, especially if it’s just routine — lunch at work, dinner if it’s there. I haven’t really been tracking it or anything.

Over the past three years, if there’s been a change, it’s not something that jumped out at me. I wouldn’t say I’ve had some major increase or loss of appetite that I’m aware of. It’s more like… food is just one of those things I get through, I guess, but I can’t point to a definite change.
Do you find yourself moving or speaking more slowly than you used to, or do you feel restless and unable to sit still?

I’m not sure I’ve noticed that in a clear way.

I mean, I don’t think anyone’s told me I’m talking slower or moving strangely slow, if that’s what you mean. With my kind of work, I’m moving around a lot anyway, so it’s hard to judge. There are times I probably feel like I’m dragging a bit, but I don’t know if that’s the same thing as moving slower than I used to.

As far as being restless, I don’t think I’m pacing around or unable to sit still. I might shift around or have trouble getting comfortable sometimes, but I wouldn’t say that’s a big thing I’ve noticed. It’s more that I’m just kind of getting through the day, not really thinking, “Oh, I’m slowed down,” or “I can’t sit still.”

So I guess my answer is… I don’t really know. Nothing obvious that I can point to.
Have you ever thought about how you would end your life if you decided to do it?

I don’t really have a clear answer to that. I mean… I’ve never sat down and worked out some specific way, if that’s what you’re asking. It’s more that when you ask it like that, I kind of freeze up because I don’t want to say the wrong thing.

I can’t point to a particular method or anything I’ve planned out. I haven’t had something where I was like, “This is exactly how I’d do it.” It’s not something I’ve mapped out in my head like that.

So… no, not in a specific way that I could describe.
Have you thought about how you would carry out ending your life if you decided to do it?

I guess… like I was trying to say, I haven’t really gotten that far with it in my head. I know that sounds maybe evasive, but I don’t mean it that way.

When you say “how I would carry it out,” I think of having steps or some kind of plan, and I don’t have that. I haven’t sat there and figured out, “Okay, I’d do this, then this,” or picked a time or place or anything like that. It’s more like… if the thought comes up, it’s vague and uncomfortable, and then I kind of push it away or get stuck feeling bad about even thinking it.

So no, I don’t have a way I’ve planned to carry it out. I can’t give you details because I really haven’t worked out details.
Have you ever come up with a specific plan for how you would end your life?

No… I don’t think I can say I’ve ever had a specific plan.

I know you’ve asked it a couple different ways, and I’m trying to answer it honestly without making it sound better or worse than it is. When I hear “specific plan,” I think of someone having it all worked out—like knowing exactly what they’d do, when, where, what steps they’d take—and I haven’t done that. I haven’t made arrangements or decided on anything like that.

I’ve had times where the subject comes into my head in a darker, more general way, but it doesn’t turn into a plan I’m preparing to follow. It’s not organized like that. It’s more uncomfortable and kind of frightening to even talk about, honestly, because I don’t want you to think I’m saying something I’m not saying.

So, to answer your question directly: no, I haven’t come up with a specific plan for how I would end my life.
Have you experienced periods of more severe depression where you felt completely unable to function?

Yeah… yes. I mean, I’m still getting up and going through the motions a lot of the time, but there have been stretches where it feels like I’m barely keeping the pieces together.

At work, especially, I’ve been missing things I normally wouldn’t miss. I do landscaping and groundskeeping, and there’s a lot of planning that goes into the day—what crew is going where, what materials we need, little details that matter. I used to be pretty solid with that, but lately I’ll overlook something or forget to follow up, and then it puts other people behind. The crew paperwork, too… I keep falling behind on it. It’s embarrassing because people are used to me being the one who has that handled, and now I’m the reason somebody else has to chase it down or cover for me.

And outside of work, I’ve pulled back from things I used to help with. There’s a community garden I was involved in, and some music gatherings I helped organize—not big professional stuff or anything, just local people getting together—but I’ve been avoiding them. I don’t return messages like I should, or I say I’ll help and then I just… don’t get there. So people have had to step in where they used to count on me.

So, completely unable to function… maybe not like I’m lying in bed every single day doing nothing, but there have definitely been times where I’m not functioning the way I need to, and it’s affecting work and people around me.
Do you find yourself fidgeting or having trouble sitting still when you're feeling down?

I’m not sure, honestly. I don’t think of myself as someone who’s constantly fidgeting or pacing when I’m feeling low, if that’s what you mean.

I mean… I might shift around in a chair or mess with my hands a little, but I don’t know if that’s more than anyone else would do when they’re uncomfortable talking about something. Sitting here, I’m probably doing it some just because this is a tense conversation. But at home or at work, I haven’t really noticed that as a big thing, like I can’t sit still or I’m driven to keep moving.

When I’m down, it feels more like I’m stuck than restless, if that makes sense. But no, I can’t say I’ve clearly noticed fidgeting or trouble sitting still as one of the main things.

Maybe right when I first get up I can tell myself, okay, let’s get moving, maybe today won’t be so bad. But it doesn’t last. And outside of work, I’ve pulled back from things I used to help with. There’s a community garden I was involved in, and some music gatherings I helped organize—not big professional stuff or anything, just local people getting together—but I’ve been avoiding them.
